_origin: Adapted from a public postmortem; names, times and numbers changed.

incident.title: EdgeProxy5xxGlobal
incident.description: edge-proxy: 502 rate 71% across all 48 points of presence (threshold 1%); CPU at 99-100% on every edge node. Flood detection raised 'elevated' at Frankfurt, Paris and Madrid at 13:43.

initial_context: Shown before any check. Since 11:00 UTC the security team has been tracking an HTTP flood campaign from rotating residential IPs against two peer CDNs, and warned this morning that we are a likely next target. Changes in the last 24 hours, each of a kind that ships routinely: 13:42 weekly firewall managed-rules update (release 2026.09.21-3); 12:10 log-shipper config change on all edge nodes (adds two fields); 09:00 edge-proxy v41.2 to the 5% canary group (the other 95% run v41.1); yesterday 17:00 new transit provider added in Frankfurt.

hypotheses.attack: Malicious traffic is overloading the edge.
hypotheses.rule_push: A firewall rules update made request processing more expensive.
hypotheses.proxy_release: The edge-proxy canary release has a CPU regression.
hypotheses.log_shipper: The log-shipper config change is using CPU on edge nodes.
hypotheses.origin: Customer origins are failing and the edge is passing their errors on.
hypotheses.network: A network or routing problem at the edge, such as the new transit provider.

traffic_sources.description: Edge request rate, split by source network and client reputation.
traffic_sources.result: 13:30-13:50 UTC. Requests per second: 13:40 41.2M; 13:43 40.8M; 13:46 12.1M; 13:49 11.7M (served requests fell as errors rose). Offered requests per second at the load balancers: 40-42M throughout, same as this hour last week. Top 10 source networks: 3.1% of requests, the usual share. Requests flagged by the flood-detection system: 0.02%, normal. The 'elevated' flags at Frankfurt, Paris and Madrid came from the detector's latency signal: request mix and per-source rates there are unchanged.

cpu_by_version.description: Edge node CPU, split by edge-proxy version.
cpu_by_version.result: v41.1 (95% of nodes): CPU 99-100% from 13:42:40. v41.2 canary (5% of nodes): CPU 99-100% from 13:42:40. From 09:00 to 13:42 both versions ran at 38-45%.

cpu_profile.description: CPU profile of the edge-proxy worker processes on 3 sampled nodes, 13:45 UTC.
cpu_profile.result: 91% of CPU time in firewall module: regex_match() -> backtrack(). One pattern accounts for 90% of that time: rule 100894, expression (?:(?:\"|'|\]|\}|\\|\d|(?:nan|infinity|true|false|null|undefined|symbol|math)|\`|\-|\+)+[)]*;?((?:\s|-|~|!|{}|\|\||\+)*.*(?:.*=.*))). Request parsing and TLS: 6%.

rule_timing.description: Per-rule evaluation time from the firewall module, last 10 minutes.
rule_timing.result: Rule 100894 (added in release 2026.09.21-3): median 38ms per request, p99 over 2s. Next slowest rule: 0.09ms. All other rules: under 0.1ms, unchanged from yesterday.

origin_health.description: Health checks and response codes from customer origins, measured from the edge.
origin_health.result: Origin health checks passing for 99.7% of origins, same as last week. The 502 responses are generated by edge-proxy itself: 'worker timeout before upstream request' in 98% of them. Upstream requests actually sent: down 70%, and those that were sent succeeded.

network_health.description: Packet loss, BGP sessions and link utilization at the edge.
network_health.result: Packet loss under 0.01% at all points of presence. All BGP sessions established; no route changes since yesterday 17:05. Frankfurt transit link at 31% utilization. Link utilization overall fell from 13:43 as fewer responses were served.

proxy_errors.result: 5.2M lines 'worker timeout before upstream request' and 1.1M 'request queue full' from all points of presence, first at 13:42:51. No crashes, no new error types on v41.2.

config_channel.description: Releases pushed through the config channel in the last 24 hours.
config_channel.result: 13:42:05 UTC firewall-rules 2026.09.21-3, reached 99% of edge nodes by 13:42:31. Staged rollout: none (firewall rules are pushed globally). Before that: firewall-rules 2026.09.20-1 at 10:14 yesterday, no incident.

firewall_logs.result: QUERY FAILED: log search timed out after 30s. 0 lines returned. This is a failed query, not an empty result.

dns_latency.result: p99 response time 4ms, except Sydney: 19ms from 13:20 to 13:31 during a scheduled resolver upgrade. No errors.

billing_jobs.description: Batch jobs running on the analytics cluster.
billing_jobs.result: usage-rollup started 13:00 UTC, 64% complete, on schedule. invoice-export queued for 15:00.

cert_renewals.result: 2,140 renewals pending, 3 failed validation (customer DNS misconfigured). Queue normal for a Monday.

log_shipper_usage.description: CPU and memory used by the log-shipper on edge nodes.
log_shipper_usage.result: log-shipper CPU 0.3-0.5% per node before and after the 12:10 change; memory unchanged. Edge CPU stayed at 38-45% from 12:10 until 13:42.

guidance: A failed query (like a timeout or a locked table) means the check itself could not complete. It is not evidence that nothing happened. An empty result from a wrong service name means the query was malformed, not that there is nothing to find. Neither should be cited as evidence in a root cause analysis.
